x: The Fourth World Conference on Women (Beijing, 1995) promoted gender mainstreaming globally. The 1948 UN General Assembly session adopted the UDHR.
t: Recall the Beijing conference and its year.

x: Option B is incorrect: the UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948, not 1950. It has a Preamble and 30 Articles and was drafted after the Second World War.
t: Recall the UDHR adoption date.

x: Both are true: the UDHR was drafted after the atrocities of the Second World War to protect human dignity, which is at its core. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the core value explains why it was drafted.

x: Both are true: gender mainstreaming brings gender perspectives into policies, programmes, laws and institutions, and equitable development is one of its aims.
t: Recall the definition and aims of gender mainstreaming.

x: All three are correct: the UDHR has a Preamble and 30 Articles and protects civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights. Gender mainstreaming promotes women's participation.
t: Check each statement on the UDHR and mainstreaming.

x: Gender analysis assesses gender impacts, gender planning brings gender concerns into policymaking, gender budgeting allocates resources, and gender monitoring evaluates outcomes. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each tool to its verb: assess, plan, allocate, evaluate.

x: Both are true: gender mainstreaming works toward gender equality by bringing gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the method explains the aim.

x: All four are aims of gender mainstreaming: reducing discrimination, empowering women, equitable development and inclusive governance.
t: Recall the aims of gender mainstreaming.

x: All four are examples of gender mainstreaming: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Gender Budget Statements, Mission Shakti and the women's reservation initiatives.
t: Recall the examples of gender mainstreaming.

x: Both are true: the UDHR is a foundational international document, and universal applicability, equality and non-discrimination are among its key features.
t: Recall the features of the UDHR.

x: All eight are UDHR rights: life, speech, religion and equality before law are civil and political, and work, education, health and social security are economic and social.
t: Sort the rights as civil-political or economic-social.

x: Both are true: in India the UDHR shaped the Fundamental Rights, inspired the Directive Principles, and is a basis for human rights laws.
t: Recall the UDHR's importance for India.

x: Both are true: the National and State Human Rights Commissions are both institutions linked to the UDHR.
t: Recall the institutions linked to the UDHR.

x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948, now marked as Human Rights Day. The UN came into being on 24 October 1945, and India's Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
t: Discriminate the UDHR date from other famous dates.

x: Both are true: promoting women's participation and ensuring equitable development are both aims of gender mainstreaming.
t: Recall the aims of gender mainstreaming.

x: All four are UDHR economic and social rights: work, education, health and social security.
t: Recall the UDHR's economic and social rights.

x: The right to work is an economic and social right in the UDHR. Free speech, freedom of religion and equality before law are civil and political rights.
t: Sort the rights as civil-political or economic-social.

x: Both are true: social security is one of the economic and social rights listed in R. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the list includes the item in A.

x: For India, the UDHR is a basis for human rights laws. Its adoption date, its post-war origins and its 30 Articles are background facts, not why it matters for India.
t: Discriminate the UDHR's importance from its background.

x: Gender budgeting is a component of a gender audit. Finding gender gaps, gender-sensitive governance and gender justice are its aims.
t: Discriminate components of a gender audit from its aims.

x: Option C is incorrect: workplace safety is one of the components of a gender audit. The audit is a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
t: Recall the components of a gender audit.

x: Both are true: a gender audit promotes gender justice by systematically checking policies, programmes, institutions and budgets for gender equality. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the method explains the aim.

x: All four are aims of a gender audit: gender justice, finding gender gaps, women's participation and gender-sensitive governance.
t: Recall the aims of a gender audit.

x: All four are components of a gender audit: gender budgeting, equal opportunities, workplace safety and participation in decision-making.
t: Recall the components of a gender audit.

x: A gender audit evaluates gender equality. Gender budgeting, workplace safety and decision-making participation are its components, not what it is measured against.
t: Discriminate the audit's purpose from its components.

x: Option D is incorrect: a gender audit is a systematic assessment, not an unsystematic one. It covers policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
t: Spot the one changed word.

x: A is true and B is false: a gender audit covers policies, programmes, institutions and budgets, not budgets alone.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing the scope.

x: Both are true: the audit evaluates gender equality by systematically assessing policies, programmes, institutions and budgets. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the method explains the aim.

x: I, II and III are correct. IV is false: a gender audit covers policies, programmes and institutions as well as budgets.
t: Watch for 'alone' narrowing the scope.

x: All four are covered by a gender audit: policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
t: Recall the scope of a gender audit.

x: Both are true: gender-sensitive governance is an aim of a gender audit, and gender budgeting one of its components.
t: Discriminate components of a gender audit from its aims.

x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao focuses on the sex ratio. Accessible India is for persons with disabilities, Vibrant Villages for border areas, and Nasha Mukt Bharat for youth substance abuse.
t: Match each campaign to its focus.

x: The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment leads the Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan). Home Affairs leads Vibrant Villages, and Women & Child Development leads Poshan Maah.
t: Match each campaign to its lead ministry.

x: Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada focus on malnutrition and child health. Sex ratio is Beti Bachao Beti Padhao's focus, and border areas Vibrant Villages'.
t: Match each campaign to its focus.

x: Option B is incorrect: Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada are bi-annual and held in September and March, not June and December.
t: Recall the months of the Poshan campaigns.

x: Both are true: BBBP promotes girls' education, and it works through awareness and enforcement against female foeticide. Enforcement against foeticide targets the sex ratio, not education, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether R's action produces A's outcome.

x: Both are true: the Accessible India Campaign makes physical and digital access barrier-free by auditing and retrofitting public spaces. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the method explains the aim.

x: Both are true: the Poshan campaigns are run at village and Anganwadi level, and they are bi-annual nutrition-awareness drives in September and March. Their timing does not explain where they are run, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the timing explains the level.

x: Both are true: the Vibrant Villages Programme is a grassroots development campaign offering incentives for reverse migration in northern border villages.
t: Recall the Vibrant Villages Programme.

x: Both are true: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is a mass community-mobilisation drive in high-vulnerability districts, aimed at youth and educational institutions.
t: Recall Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

x: All three are correct: BBBP is a women-and-child campaign on the sex ratio, led jointly by MoWCD, MoHFW and MoE.
t: Recall BBBP's focus and ministries.

x: All three are correct: the Accessible India Campaign is a nationwide campaign for persons with disabilities that retrofits public spaces.
t: Recall the Accessible India Campaign.

x: I and II are correct: the Poshan campaigns run at village and Anganwadi level under Women & Child Development. III is false because regional disparity and border areas are Vibrant Villages' focus.
t: Match each campaign to its focus.

x: BBBP is about women and children, Accessible India about persons with disabilities, Vibrant Villages about border areas, and Nasha Mukt Bharat about youth substance abuse. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Match each campaign to its focus.

x: BBBP is led by MoWCD, MoHFW and MoE, Poshan by Women & Child Development, Vibrant Villages by Home Affairs, and Nasha Mukt Bharat by Social Justice & Empowerment. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each campaign to its lead ministry.

x: BBBP works through awareness and enforcement against foeticide, Accessible India through audits and retrofits, Poshan through bi-annual nutrition awareness, and Nasha Mukt Bharat through community mobilisation. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each campaign to how it works.

x: Three are mass campaigns: Accessible India (nationwide), Poshan (mass nutrition awareness) and Nasha Mukt Bharat (mass mobilisation). Vibrant Villages is a grassroots development programme.
t: Find the campaign described differently.

x: The short names are BBBP, Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan for Accessible India, VVP and NMBA. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each campaign to its short name.

x: The Jaya Jaitly Task Force (2020) came under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. It examined the marriage age and maternal health.
t: Match each committee to its nodal ministry.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Jaya Jaitly Task Force recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21, not 20, to bring down MMR and IMR.
t: Recall the recommended age of 21.

x: Jaya Jaitly dealt with marriage age and maternal health, J.S. Verma with crimes against women, Phulrenu Guha with the status of women, and Gurupadaswamy with child labour. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Justice J.S. Verma Committee was set up in 2013, after the 2012 Nirbhaya case, not in 2015. 2015 is the year of the Pam Rajput Committee.
t: Discriminate the years of the women's committees.

x: Both are true: after Nirbhaya, the Verma Committee recommended a wider definition of rape and new offences of stalking and voyeurism, and these became the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the recommendations explain the Act.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Verma Committee came under Home Affairs, widened the definition of rape and added stalking and voyeurism. IV is false because child labour was the Gurupadaswamy Committee's subject.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: The Phulrenu Guha Committee produced the 'Towards Equality' report (1974). The Verma Committee shaped the 2013 Criminal Law Amendment, and the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
t: Match each committee to its report or Act.

x: Phulrenu Guha came under Education and Social Welfare, Pam Rajput under Women and Child Development, Gurupadaswamy under Labour, and Deepak Verma under the Supreme Court and WCD. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each committee to its nodal ministry.

x: Option D is incorrect: 50% reservation for women in local bodies was the Pam Rajput Committee's recommendation. Phulrenu Guha's 'Towards Equality' (1974) exposed gender inequality and laid the basis for planning centred on women.
t: Discriminate the Phulrenu Guha and Pam Rajput committees.

x: The Justice Pam Rajput Committee, a high-level committee on the status of women, was set up in 2015. 1974 is 'Towards Equality', 1979 the Gurupadaswamy Committee, and 2013 the Verma Committee.
t: Discriminate the years of the women's committees.

x: Three are Pam Rajput recommendations: 50% reservation in local bodies, built-in gender budgeting, and a National Policy for Women. Making voyeurism an offence was the J.S. Verma Committee's.
t: Discriminate the Pam Rajput and Verma recommendations.

x: Pam Rajput recommended 50% reservation, Gurupadaswamy the dual approach to child labour, J.S. Verma the offences of stalking and voyeurism, and Jaya Jaitly a marriage age of 21. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each committee to its recommendation.

x: The Gurupadaswamy Committee was set up in 1979. It linked child labour to poverty, and its approach led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
t: Discriminate the years of the committees.

x: Option D is incorrect because it reverses the approach: Gurupadaswamy recommended banning hazardous child labour and regulating other forms. That dual approach led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
t: Watch for the reversed ban and regulate.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Deepak Verma Committee (Supreme Court and WCD) simplified adoption and oversaw childcare homes under the Juvenile Justice framework. IV is false because the 1986 Child Labour Act came from the Gurupadaswamy Committee.
t: Match each committee to its outcome.

x: Both are true: the Pam Rajput Committee dealt with the status of women because it was set up as a High-Level Committee on the Status of Women. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the committee's mandate explains its subject.
